messages:
nina: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tenant-local policy cache for console queries (subscribe + deltas) instead of per-request RPCs to control-plane.
nina: idea is to reduce repeated authz RPCs for high-frequency dashboard polling while keeping revokes fast via a small invalidate channel.
kevin: how small is "small invalidate channel"? you mean push invalidation events only, not full policy blobs?
nina: yes. control-plane pushes compact deltas (policy ids + nonce updates). full sync happens on startup or on cache-miss.
olga: what's the expected memory footprint per tenant? dashboards for some customers spawn thousands of short-lived actors.
ben: rough estimate: ~2-8KB per tenant for policy index + rules pointers. worst-case tenants with huge role graphs might be larger — we should cap and fall back to server-side checks.
kevin: fall back path sounds necessary. fallback triggers: (a) cache eviction, (b) missed delta > 2s, (c) tenant size over threshold.
ben: agreed. add a circuit-breaker: when fallback_rate > 0.5% over 10m for a tenant, degrade to sync-mode for that tenant and alert.
olga: question on consistency: how do we handle urgent revokes (legal takedown) i.e., zero-window? deltas might be lost or delayed.
nina: two mechanisms: (1) a high-priority revoke topic that bypasses queueing (push-through), and (2) a sync invalidation endpoint in control-plane that increments tenant nonce to force next token/lookup to fail.
kevin: operationally, do we want signed tokens or purely local verification? signed tokens help when console sits in front of other proxies.
nina: tokens are optional. design allows token-less caches; verifier component can consult local cache. tokens are useful for cross-service calls (embedding service -> console).
ben: perf numbers from bench: local cache p99 for authz check ~1.8ms vs remote RPC ~22ms (network+policy-eval). end-to-end dashboard p99 improved ~60-80ms in our microbench.
olga: nice. but we must measure memory and CPU under churn. can we add synthetic churn test to perf harness?
kevin: yes. I'll add tenant-churn scenarios to the existing console perf job (5k tenants, varying churn).
nina: config sketch (defaults conservative):
```
console.auth_cache:
  mode: subscriber
  delta_buffer_ms: 200
  max_tenant_cache_kb: 64
  eviction_policy: lru
  high_priority_revoke_topic: true
  fallback_circuit_breaker_threshold: 0.005
```
ben: canary plan: start with non-critical tenants (internal + 3 small customers). 5% traffic for 1h, monitor authz.cache.hit_rate, authz.fallback_rate, dashboard.p99. abort if fallback_rate spike or revoke latency > 500ms.
olga: add an alert: page on revoke_latency > 200ms for >30s for any tenant. legal takedowns must not be delayed.
ci-bot: perf-job scheduled: console-auth-cache-churn -> 2026-04-05T15:00Z -> 4h run.
kevin: implementation notes: make delta protocol idempotent, include sequence numbers + signatures. use gRPC stream with keepalive and backpressure.
nina: also ensure metrics: per-tenant cache_size_kb, delta_lag_ms, revoke_latency_ms. correlate with dashboard traces.
ben: I'll prototype subscriber in go; keep it as a separate component initially to avoid coupling; later we can embed sidecar in console service.
nina: thanks. can we aim for a small spike-free canary by next sprint? I'll draft the PR with the config and checklist.
kevin: ok. include rollback steps: disable subscriber mode, trigger full sync, and enable sync-only path.
olga: +1. please include test for the revoke hot-path.
ben: will do.
ci-bot: Canary toggle created: auth-cache-subscriber -> feature-flag -> rollout group: internal-devs+3-customers.
